posts.content_md:
I know next to zero when it comes to chemistry so please forgive if this is an obvious question...

Is there a simple off-the-shelf kind of way to calibrate a PH meter? I have one I've purchased off eBay but don't trust it since it's used and don't know of a way to check its output.

All of the references on the web talk about using a two-point system for calibrating a meter but as those require solutions of a specific PH and I haven't seen them for sale, I'm not sure where to start.

Any thoughts?

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: B3 is still friends however I no longer work there, but the calibrations solutions work very well. You can use a one point calibration if you are on a budget and you are testing near 4 or 7. Otherwise use two points. You will need to know how to put your pH meter into calibration mode.
